Synopsis:
    Nearly a third of India's coal-fired power plants (59 as of Sept 9, up from 45 end-August) are running critically low on coal stocks, driven by sustained peak electricity demand (~267 GW) amid El Niño heat. Solar covers daytime load but inadequate battery storage and low reservoir levels increase pressure on coal generation. Coal India is ramping up rail and road deliveries to utilities, holding ~76 Mt at pitheads. Short-term risk centres on whether logistics can keep pace with demand before stocks deteriorate further.

Q01. Is the content's main message about EU energy, EU commodities, German power market prices, German energy economics?
Relevance: NO — The article is exclusively focused on India's domestic coal and power supply situation. No EU, TTF, or German market angle.

Q02. Is the content confirming already known information or reporting very new/uncertain risks?
Risk score: 25 — India's seasonal coal stress during summer heat waves is a recurring, well-documented pattern. The uptick in critical plants (59 vs 45) adds a fresh data point but is broadly in line with known El Niño demand dynamics. Not a surprising development.
